title: Goddyn's conjecture on thin spanning trees

statement.text: A spanning tree of a graph ''G'' is called <math>\epsilon</math>-'''thin''' if it contains at most an <math>\epsilon</math> fraction of the edges of each cut. Is there a function <math>f: (0,1)\to {\mathbb Z}_+</math> such that every <math>f(\epsilon)</math>-edge-connected graph has an <math>\epsilon</math>-thin spanning tree?
